The Luo are a ___E:Nilotic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples)___ -speaking ethnic group native to ___E:western Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyanza_Province)___ and the ___E:Mara Region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mara_Region)___ of northern ___E:Tanzania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania)___ .

The Luo are the fourth-largest ethnic group (10.65%) in Kenya, after the ___E:Kikuyu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people)___ (17.13%), the ___E:Luhya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhya_people)___ (14.35%), and the ___E:Kalenjin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people)___ (13.37%).

The Tanzanian Luo population was estimated at 1.1 million in 2001 and 3.4 million in 2020.  They are part of a larger group of related ___E:Luo peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_peoples)___ who inhabit an area ranging from ___E:South Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan)___ , southwestern ___E:Ethiopia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia)___ , northern and eastern ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ , southwestern ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ , and northern ___E:Tanzania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania)___ , making them one of the largest ethnic groups in East Africa.

They speak the ___E:Luo language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_dialect)___ , also known as Dholuo , which belongs to the ___E:Western Nilotic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Nilotic)___ branch of the ___E:Nilotic language family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_languages)___ .
Dholuo shares considerable similarities with languages spoken by other ___E:Luo peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_peoples)___ .
The Luo moved into western Kenya from Uganda between the 15th and 20th centuries in four waves.

They were closely related to ___E:Luo peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_peoples)___ found in ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ , especially the ___E:Acholi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acholi_people)___ and ___E:Padhola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padhola)___ people.
As they moved into Kenya and Tanzania, they underwent significant genetic and cultural modifications as they encountered other communities that were long established in the region.

Traditionally, Luo people practiced a mixed economy of ___E:cattle pastoralism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism)___ , seed farming and ___E:fishing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing)___ supplemented by hunting.
Today, the Luo comprise a significant fraction of ___E:East Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa)___ 's intellectual and skilled labour force in various professions.
They also engage in various trades, such as tenant fishing, small-scale farming, and urban work. [citation needed]

Luo people and people of Luo descent have made significant contributions to modern culture and civilization. ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ and Nigel N. Mwangi were key figures in the ___E:African Nationalist struggle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_nationalism)___ .

Luo scientists, such as ___E:Thomas Risley Odhiambo Nandy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thomas_Risley_Odhiambo_Nandy&action=edit&redlink=1)___ (founder of the ___E:International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (ICIPE) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Centre_of_Insect_Physiology_and_Ecology)___ and winner of ___E:UNESCO's Albert Einstein Gold Medal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_Albert_Einstein_medal)___ in 1991) and ___E:Washington Yotto Ochieng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Yotto_Ochieng)___ (winner of the Harold Spencer-Jones Gold Medal in 2019 from The ___E:Royal Institute of Navigation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_Navigation)___ (RIN)) have achieved international acclaim for their contributions.

Prof. ___E:Richard S. Odingo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Samson_Odingo)___ was the vice chairman of the ___E:Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergovernmental_Panel_on_Climate_Change)___ when it received the ___E:Nobel Peace Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize)___ in 2007 with ___E:Al Gore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore)___ .  ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , the first black ___E:President of the United States of America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States_of_America)___ and a ___E:Nobel Peace Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize)___ winner, was born to a Kenyan Luo father, ___E:Barack Obama Sr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.)___  ___E:Lupita Nyong'o U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupita_Nyong%27o)___ became the first black African to win an ___E:Academy Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress)___ in 2014.
The Luo are the originators of a number of popular music genres including ___E:benga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benga_music)___ and ___E:ohangla U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohangla)___ .
Benga is one of Africa's most popular genres.

The present day homeland of Kenyan and Tanzanian Luo lies in the eastern ___E:Lake Victoria basin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria_Basin)___ - Nam Lolwe in the former ___E:Nyanza province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyanza_province)___ in Western Kenya and the ___E:Mara region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mara_region)___ in northwestern Tanzania.
This area falls within ___E:tropical latitudes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropics)___ and straddles the ___E:equator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equator)___ .
This area also receives average rainfall levels.
The average altitudes range between 3700 and 6000 feet above sea level.
Luo people of Kenya and Tanzania form the majority of ___E:Nilotic peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples)___ .
During the British colonial period, they were known as ___E:Nilotic Kavirondo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kavirondo)___ .

The exact location of origin of the ___E:Nilotic peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples)___ is controversial but most ethnolinguists and historians place their origins between ___E:Bahr-el-Ghazal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahr_el_Ghazal_(region_of_South_Sudan))___ and ___E:Eastern Equatoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Equatoria)___ in ___E:South Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan)___ .
They practiced a mixed economy of cattle pastoralism, fishing and seed cultivation.

Some of the earliest archaeological findings on record, which describe a similar culture to this from the same region, are found at ___E:Kadero U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kadero_(archaeological_site))___ , 48 kilometres (30 miles) north of ___E:Khartoum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khartoum)___ in ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan)___ , and date to 3000 BC. Kadero contains the remains of a cattle pastoralist culture as well as a cemetery with skeletal remains featuring Sub-Saharan African phenotypes.
It also contains evidence of other animal domestication, artistry, long-distance trade, seed cultivation and fish consumption.

Genetic and linguistic studies have demonstrated that ___E:Nubian people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nubian_people)___ in Northern Sudan and Southern Egypt are an admixed group that started off as a population closely related to ___E:Nilotic peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples)___ .
This population later received significant gene flow from ___E:Middle Eastern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_eastern_people)___ and other East African populations.

Nubians are considered to be descendants of the early inhabitants of the Nile valley who later formed the ___E:Kingdom of Kush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Kush)___ which included ___E:Kerma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerma)___ and ___E:Meroe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meroe)___ and the medieval christian kingdoms of ___E:Makuria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makuria)___ , ___E:Nobatia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobatia)___ and ___E:Alodia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alodia)___ .
These studies suggest that populations closely related to Nilotic people long inhabited the Nile valley as far as Southern Egypt in antiquity.

For various reasons, slow and multi-generational migrations of Nilotic ___E:Luo Peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_peoples)___ occurred from ___E:South Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan)___ into ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ and western ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ from at least 1000 AD continuing up until the early 20th century.

Some authors note that the early phases of this expansion coincide with the collapse of the Christian Nubian kingdoms of ___E:Makuria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makuria)___ and ___E:Alodia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alodia)___ , the penetration of Arabs into central ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan)___ as well as ___E:Nilotic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples)___ adoption of ___E:Iron Age technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Iron_Age)___ .

The northern most group of ___E:Luo peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_peoples)___ - the ___E:Shilluk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shilluk_people)___ - advanced north along the ___E:White Nile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Nile)___ in the 16th century, conquering territory as far as modern day Khartoum.
They established the ___E:Shilluk Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shilluk_Kingdom)___ .

In the 15th century, ___E:Luo peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_peoples)___ moved into the ___E:Bunyoro-Kitara Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunyoro-Kitara)___ and established the ___E:Babiito dynasty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babiito_dynasty)___ in ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ .
This group assimilated into ___E:Bantu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_peoples)___ culture.

The Luo of ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ and ___E:Tanzania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania)___ are classified as ___E:Southern Luo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Luo)___ .  and are the only 'river lake Nilotes' having migrated and lived along the ___E:Nile river U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_river)___ .

They entered Kenya and Tanzania via ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ from the ___E:Bahr el-Ghazal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahr_el_Ghazal_(region_of_South_Sudan))___ region in ___E:South Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan)___ .

The Luo speakers who migrated into Kenya were chiefly from four Luo-speaking groups: the ___E:Acholi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acholi_people)___ , ___E:Adhola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adhola_people)___ and ___E:Alur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alur_people)___ people (From ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ and parts of ___E:South Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan)___ and ___E:Eastern Congo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo)___ ), especially ___E:Acholi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acholi_people)___ and ___E:Padhola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padhola)___ .

It is estimated that Dholuo has 90% lexical similarity with Lep Alur ( ___E:Alur language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alur_language)___ ); 83% with Lep Achol ( ___E:Acholi language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acholi_language)___ ); 93% with Dhopadhola (Padhola language), 74% with ___E:Anuak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anuak_language)___ , and 69% with Jurchol ( ___E:Luwo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luwo)___ ) and Dhi-Pari (Pari).

Luo of Kenya and Tanzania are also called Joluo or Jonagi / Onagi(a person who has his six lower teeth removed as a rite of passage during puberty) , singular Jaluo , Jaonagi or Joramogi / Nyikwaramogi , meaning "Ramogi's heirs." The Luo clans of Kenya and Tanzania were called Ororo , while among the Nuer they were called Liel .
In the Dinka tribe, the Luo are called the Jur-Chol .
The present-day Kenya Luo traditionally consist of 27 tribes, each in turn composed of various clans and sub-clans  ("Jo-" indicates "people of").
Oral history and genealogical evidence have been used to estimate timelines of Luo expansion into and within Kenya and Tanzania.

Four major waves of migrations into the former ___E:Nyanza province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyanza_province)___ in ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ are discernible, starting with the People of Jok ( Joka Jok ), which is estimated to have begun around 1490–1517.  Joka Jok were the first and largest wave of migrants into northern ___E:Nyanza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyanza_Province)___ .
These migrants settled at a place called Ramogi Hill, then expanded around Northern ___E:Nyanza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyanza_Province)___ .
The People of Owiny' ( Jok'Owiny ) and the People of Omolo ( Jok'Omolo ) followed soon after (1598–1625).
A miscellaneous group composed of the Suba, Sakwa, Asembo, Uyoma and Kano then followed.
The ___E:Suba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suba_people_(Kenya))___ originally were Bantu-speaking people who assimilated into Luo culture.

They fled from the ___E:Buganda Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buganda_Kingdom)___ in ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ after the civil strife that followed the murder of the 24th ___E:Kabaka of Buganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabaka_of_Buganda)___ in the mid 18th century and settled in ___E:South Nyanza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Nyanza)___ , especially at ___E:Rusinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rusinga_Island)___ and ___E:Mfangano U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mfangano_Island)___ islands.

Luo speakers crossed ___E:Winam Gulf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winam_Gulf)___ of Lake Victoria from Northern Nyanza into ___E:South Nyanza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Nyanza)___ starting in the early 17th century.
As Luo speakers migrated deeper into western Kenya, they encountered the descendants of various people who had long occupied the region.

The Great Lakes region has been inhabited since the early Stone Age.  The Kanysore culture, located at Gogo falls in ___E:Migori county U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migori_County)___ , are thought to be the first ___E:hunter gatherers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_gatherers)___ in East Africa to produce ceramics.  ___E:Twa people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twa_people)___ are thought to have created the rock art present on ___E:Mfangano Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mfangano_Island)___ .  ___E:Bantu speakers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_peoples)___ , early migrants from ___E:West Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Africa)___ , are thought to have reached western Kenya by 1000 BC. They brought with them iron-forging technology and novel farming techniques, turning the great lakes region into one of Africa's main population centres and earliest iron smelting regions.
The ___E:Urewe culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urewe)___ was dominant from 650 BC to 550 BC. This culture was found in northern Nyanza.

Bantu speaking groups found in the Lake Victoria basin today include the ___E:Luhya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhya_people)___ , ___E:Suba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suba_people_(Kenya))___ , ___E:Kunta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunta_people)___ , ___E:Kuria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuria_people)___ and ___E:Kisii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisii_people)___ . ___E:Southern Nilotic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Nilotic)___ speakers, the ___E:Nandi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandi_people)___ , ___E:Kipsigis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipsigis_people)___ and ___E:Maasai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people)___ also were found in this area.
Luo expansion into these already inhabited areas led to trade, conflict, conquest, inter-marriage and cultural assimilation.
The previous inhabitants were pushed by Luo speakers to their present day boundaries.
The Luhya were pushed up into higher ground.
The Kuria were pushed southwards between the Kenyan and Tanzania border.
The ___E:Nandi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandi_people)___ and ___E:Kipsigis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipsigis_people)___ were pushed east and northeast.

Oral histories tend to focus on the battles more than the negotiations, peaceful accommodations, and opportunistic identity-switching that surely have been no less real as the ancestors of present-day Luo moved south, established a reputation as brave fighters and successful strategists, attracted women and youth from threatened or subjugated groups, and found their numbers swelling to the present size of millions
As Luo people moved into the Nyanza region, the local Bantu peoples stopped circumcising as they increasingly adopted Luo culture.
Women played a significant role in overcoming prohibitions to intermarriage by changing circumcision practices and other customs.

Luo women told the local Bantu men, "If you want to marry us you have to stop circumcising and file your bottom teeth, so that you look like us and we can marry you." The Suba and other Bantu groups were interested in Luo brides because their bridewealth was much lower or non-existent.
Luo women living in Suba communities spoke to their children in Luo, who became bilingual.
The Luo language spread rapidly this way.
Luo customs and habits also changed as they adopted the culture of the communities with which they interacted.

Conflict and raids in this diverse area led to the development of defensive savanna architecture, typified by the stone walled ruins, ___E:Thimlich Ohinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thimlich_Ohinga)___ in South Nyanza.  ___E:Neville Chittick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neville_Chittick)___ , the director of the British Institute of History and Archaeology in East Africa was the first to assert that the site was likely to have been constructed before the arrival of Luo speakers.
This assertion is poorly supported archaeologically, however, because most of the stone walled structures are dated to within the period of Luo expansion.

Nevertheless, Luo speakers maintained ___E:Thimlich Ohinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thimlich_Ohinga)___ and continued the tradition of building stone walled fortresses ( Ohingni ) as well as defensive earthworks ( Gunda Bur ) in both Northern and Southern Nyanza.
These defensive earth works would curve around living areas surrounding them. Some of these defensive structures enclosed several hundred houses.
Archaeological and ethnographic analyses of the sites have shown that the spatial organisation of these structures most closely resembles the layout of traditional Luo homesteads.
Ceramic analysis also confirms continuity between the earliest inhabitants of these sites and Luo speakers.
With the arrival of the Europeans, these sites were slowly vacated as colonial administration established peace in the region.

The families living in the enclosures moved out into individual homesteads using ___E:euphorbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphorbia)___ instead of stone as fencing material. ___E:A fence is a structure that encloses an area, typically outdoors creating a boundary, and is usually constructed from posts that are connected by boards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fence)___ .
By the mid-20th century, they were all abandoned.
Early ___E:British U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire)___ contact with the Luo was indirect and sporadic.

Relations intensified only when the completion of the ___E:Uganda Railway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Railway)___ had confirmed British intentions and largely removed the need for local alliances.

In 1896, a ___E:punitive expedition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punitive_expedition)___ was mounted in support of the Wanga ruler ___E:Mumia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rulers_of_Wanga)___ in Ugenya against the Kager clan led by ___E:Ochieng Ger III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gero_(Luo_leader)&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , otherwise known as Gero. Over 200 were quickly killed by a ___E:Maxim gun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_gun)___ .

Another 300 people in the Uyoma resistance were killed by an expedition led by Sir Charles Horbley (Bwana Obila Muruayi) when they were confiscating Luo cattle to help feed the Indian workers who were building the Uganda railway.
Following these clashes, Luo spiritual leaders advised the people to actively cooperate with the British.
By 1900, the Luo chief Odera was providing 1,500 porters for a British expedition against the ___E:Nandi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandi_people)___ .
The British set up regional headquarters first at ___E:Mumias U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumias)___ then at ___E:Kisumu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu)___ .
They worked to submit the Luo to colonial control and administration.
Within a few decades, traditional leaders and political structures were replaced by colonial chiefs.

The Seventh-day Adventist Church missionaries were amongst the earliest Christian missionaries to proselytise to Luo people. ___E:Arthur Carscallen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Carscallen)___ , a Canadian ___E:Seventh-day Adventist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh-day_Adventist)___ (SDA) was the first Adventist to work in Kenya with Peter Nyambo, from ___E:Nyasaland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyasaland)___ (Present day Malawi).
The first mission was opened with the assistance of German missionary Abraham C. Enns, in November 1906 at Gendia Hill, ___E:Kendu Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendu_Bay)___ .

These missionaries established stations at Wire Hill, ___E:Rusinga Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rusinga_Island)___ , Kanyadoto, Karung, ___E:Kisii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisii,_Kenya)___ and Kamagambo.
These were all in ___E:South Nyanza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Nyanza)___ .
The first Luo SDA converts were baptised on 21 May 1911. Carscallen was the first to reduce ___E:Dholuo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dholuo)___ to writing.
He produced a textbook of grammar and started translating the bible into Dholuo.

Catholic missionaries and Anglican missionaries through the ___E:Church Mission Society (CMS) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Mission_Society)___ were also active throughout Nyanza, but mainly focused on Northern Nyanza.
It remains unclear whether Luo people westernised due to colonial pressure or they readily accepted aspects of western culture.
However, by the 1930s, the Luo way of life had changed significantly and westernized.

Some suggest that the efforts of Chiefs ( Ruoth ) such as Odera Akang'o played a role in this. In 1915, the ___E:Colonial Government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_Africa)___ sent Odera Akang'o , the ruoth of Gem, to ___E:Kampala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala)___ , Uganda.
He was impressed by the British settlement there and upon his return home he initiated a forced process of adopting western styles of "schooling, dress and hygiene".

This resulted in the rapid education of the Luo in the English language and English ways.  European education carried out by the Christian missionaries also played a role in the westernization of the Luo.
The apparent acquiescence to British colonial rule was shattered by a movement known as ___E:Mumboism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumboism)___ that took root in South Nyanza.

In 1913, Onyango Dunde of central Kavirondo proclaimed to have been sent by the serpent goddes of ___E:Lake Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria)___ , Mumbo to spread his teachings.
The colonial government recognized this movement as a threat to their authority because of the Mumbo creed.
Mumbo pledged to drive out the colonialists and their supporters and condemned their religion.

Since violent resistance had been proven to be futile as the Africans were outmatched technologically, this movement focused on anticipating the end of colonialism, rather than actively inducing it. This movement was classified as a ___E:millennialist cult U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennialism)___ . ___E:Mumboism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumboism)___ spread amongst the Luo and the ___E:Kisii people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisii_people)___ .
The Colonial authorities suppressed the movement by deporting and imprisoning adherents in the 1920s and 1930s.

The earliest modern African political organization in ___E:Kenya Colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony)___ sought to protest pro-settler policies, and increased taxes on Africans and the despised Kipande (Identifying metal band worn around the neck).

Mass meetings were organized separately by Luo people in ___E:Kavirondo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kavirondo)___ and the ___E:Kikuyu people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people)___ in ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ .
A strike at the CMS mission school in ___E:Maseno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maseno)___ was organised by Daudi Basudde.

He raised concerns about the damaging implications on African land ownership by switching from the ___E:East African Protectorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_African_Protectorate)___ to the ___E:Kenya Colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony)___ .

A series of meetings dubbed Piny Owacho (Voice of the People) culminated in a large mass meeting held in December 1921 advocating for individual title deeds, getting rid of the Kipande system and a fairer tax system.

Bound by the same concerns, ___E:James Beauttah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Beauttah)___ , one of the founders of the ___E:Kikuyu Central Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_Central_Association)___ initiated an alliance between the Kikuyu and Luo communities.
Archdeacon W. E.

Owen, an ___E:Anglican missionary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_Missionary)___ and prominent advocate for African affairs, formalised and canalised the Piny' Owacho (Voice of the People) movement.
Colonial authorities would come to praise him as having re-directed the political movement, which was thought of as premature.
However, locals perceived him as their advocate.
He started the Kavirondo Taxpayers Welfare Association and became its president, offering Africans an avenue through which they could address their grievances.
However, he concentrated primarily on welfare issues and avoided politics that would upset colonial authorities.

___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ started the Luo Thrift and Trading Corporation (LUTATCO) after noting that Luo business owners, who were the most financially independent Africans, loathed education.
He also sought to uplift the economic status of the Luo community whilst proving that education was useful for business.

The LUTATCO office was the first African owned building in ___E:Kisumu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu)___ Town. One of the many business ventures it engaged in included the publication of African Nationalist newspapers including ___E:Achieng Oneko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achieng_Oneko)___ 's vernacular newspaper Ramogi and ___E:Paul Ngei U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Ngei)___ 's radical newspaper Uhuru Wa Africa .

For his efforts he was appointed as 'Ker' or Chief of the ___E:Luo Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_Union_(Welfare_Organisation))___ , an organisation that represented the interests of the greater Luo Peoples in East Africa.
Oginga Odinga would become a Key political figure in Kenya.

He first ventured into politics when he joined the ___E:Kenya African Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_African_Union)___ . ___E:Harry Thuku U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Thuku)___ , a pioneering Kikuyu politician, founded the Kenya African Study Union in 1944 which later became the ___E:Kenya African Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_African_Union)___ .

This was an African nationalist organisation that demanded amongst other things, access to white owned land. It was multitribal. ___E:Jomo Kenyatta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta)___ became president of KAU in 1947. In an effort to gain nationwide support of KAU, ___E:Jomo Kenyatta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta)___ visited ___E:Kisumu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu)___ in 1952. His effort to build up support for KAU in Nyanza inspired ___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ , the Ker (chief) of the ___E:Luo Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_Union_(Welfare_Organisation))___ to join KAU and delve into politics.

The Luo generally were not dispossessed of their land by white settlers, avoiding the fate that befell the pastoral ethnic groups inhabiting the Kenyan " ___E:White Highlands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Highlands)___ ".

Many Luo played significant roles in the struggle for Kenyan independence, but the people were relatively uninvolved in the ___E:Mau Mau Uprising U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_Uprising)___ (1952–60).
Instead, they used their education to advance the cause of independence peacefully.

An intense propaganda campaign by the colonial government effectively discouraged other Kenyan communities, settlers and the international community from sympathising with the movement by emphasising on real and perceived acts of barbarism perpetrated by the Mau Mau. Although a much smaller number of Europeans lost their lives compared to Africans during the uprising, each individual European loss of life was publicised in disturbing detail, emphasising elements of betrayal and bestiality.
As a result, the protest was mainly supported by the ___E:Kikuyu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people)___ who began the uprising.

Luo supporters of Mau Mau and those deemed by the colonial government to support it were imprisoned as well. Most notably, ___E:Ramogi Achieng Oneko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramogi_Achieng_Oneko)___ , a KAU leader and one of the ___E:Kapenguria six U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria_Six)___ . ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ 's grandfather, ___E:Hussein Onyango Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hussein_Onyango_Obama)___ , was involved in the African nationalist movement.
He was imprisoned and tortured by the colonial authorities on suspicions that he was involved in the Mau Mau rebellion.

Luo lawyer ___E:Argwings Kodhek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.M.G._Argwings-Kodhek)___ , the first East African to obtain a law degree, became known as the Mau Mau lawyer as he would successfully defend Africans accused of ___E:Mau Mau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_rebellion)___ crimes pro bono.

Following the suppression of the Mau Mau uprising and containment of Kikuyu politicians, Luo anticolonial activists filled the gap, achieving prominence on the political scene. ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ stepped into the limelight and became one of the major figures in the struggle for Kenya's independence.

His intelligence, discipline, oratory and organisational skills set him apart. ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ started the Kenya Federation of Labour (KFL), which quickly became the most active political body in Kenya, representing all the trade unions.
Mboya's successes in trade unionism earned him respect and admiration.

Mboya established international connections, particularly with labour leaders in the ___E:United States of America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_America)___ through the ___E:International Confederation of Free Trade Unions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Confederation_of_Free_Trade_Unions)___ (ICFTU).

He used these connections and his international celebrity status to counter moves by the colonial government   Tom Mboya started the ___E:Nairobi People's Convention Party (NPCP) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_People%27s_Convention_Party)___ , inspired by ___E:Kwame Nkurumah's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah)___ ___E:People's Convention Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Convention_Party)___ .
It became the most organised and effective political party in the country.

It later merged with the ___E:Kenya Independence Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Independence_Movement)___ and KAU to form the ___E:Kenya African National Union (KANU) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_African_National_Union)___ , which would go on to rule the country until 2002. Tom Mboya also started the ___E:Kennedy Airlift U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kennedy_Airlift)___ scholarship program in order to address the issue of a lack of African skilled labour.

Over 800 Kenyans and East Africans benefited from this program, including environmentalist and ___E:Nobel Peace Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize)___ winner ___E:Wangari Maathai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wangari_Maathai)___ , former vice president ___E:George Saitoti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Saitoti)___ and ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ 's father, ___E:Barack Obama Sr U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr)___ .

The first election for African Members of the Legislative Council (MLCs) was in 1957. ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ and ___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ were elected.

In June 1958, ___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ called for the release of ___E:Jomo Kenyatta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta)___ who had been imprisoned following the crackdown on the Mau Mau uprising.
He made this call at a Legislative council debate.

He endured months of persecution for taking this stand before it became the rallying call for the African nationalist movement.  ___E:The Lancaster House Conferences U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancaster_House_Conferences_(Kenya))___ were held in London to discuss Kenya's independence and constitutional framework.

Tom Mboya and Oginga Odinga enlisted the assistance of ___E:Thurgood Marshall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thurgood_Marshall)___ , an American Lawyer and civil rights activist to draft the first constitution.

After Kenya became independent on 12 December 1963, ___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ declined the presidency of Kenya and agreed to assume the vice presidency with ___E:Jomo Kenyatta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta)___ as the head of government.
Their administration represented the ___E:Kenya African National Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_African_National_Union)___ (KANU) party.

The Luo and the Kikuyu inherited the bulk of political power in the first years following Kenya's independence in 1963.  However, differences with Kenyatta caused Odinga to defect from the party and abandon the vice presidency in 1966. ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ political intrigues were at play in local Kenyan politics.

The ___E:western U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Bloc)___ and ___E:eastern blocs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bloc)___ actively sought to influence local policy making and win allies resulting in a proxy cold war in Kenya.
Local politics became enmeshed with cold war ideological divisions.

Odinga and ___E:Bildad Kaggia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bildad_Kaggia)___ , a Kikuyu politician and ___E:Mau Mau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_rebellion)___ leader, criticised the Kenyatta government for adopting a corrupt land redistribution policy that did not benefit the poor and landless. ___E:Pio Gama Pinto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pio_Gama_Pinto)___ , a prominent anti-colonial activist, Odinga's chief tactician and link to the eastern bloc was assassinated on 25 February 1965 in what is recognised as Kenya's first political assassination.

Odinga became increasingly sidelined in government and was eventually compelled to resign and start his own political party – the ___E:Kenya People's Union (KPU) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_People%27s_Union)___ .
The ___E:Kenya People's Union (KPU) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_People%27s_Union)___ had strong support amongst the Luo.  The Kenyatta government persecuted this party.

A security Act was passed in Parliament in July 1966 that permitted the government to carry out detention without trial ostensibly to maintain law and order in situations where the current order was threatened.
This Act was immediately used against KPU members.

In August 1966, government police arrested prominent Luo KPU members including ___E:Ochola Mak'Anyengo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ochola_Ogaye_Mak%27Anyengo)___ (the secretary general of the Kenya Petroleum Oil Workers Union), Oluande Koduol (Oginga Odinga's private secretary) and Peter Ooko (the general secretary of the East African Common Services Civil Servants Union) and detained without trial.
The ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ intrigues reached their peak in 1969. Since Odinga's exit from KANU, the Luo increasingly became politically marginalised.

Argwings Kodhek, the pioneering Mau Mau lawyer died in a car crash under mysterious circumstances on 29 January 1969. ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ , widely touted as the heir apparent to Kenyatta, was assassinated 6 months after on 5 July 1969. The political tension led to the ___E:Kisumu massacre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu_massacre)___ when Kenyatta's presidential guard and police forces shot and killed several civilians in ___E:Kisumu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu)___ Town, the capital of ___E:Nyanza Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyanza_Province)___ .
Following this massacre, KPU was banned, turning Kenya into a de facto one party state.
All KPU members were arrested and detained without trial, including ___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ .
The political marginalisation of Nyanza province worsened and continued under the ___E:Moi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_arap_Moi)___ administration.

___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ was released from detention in 1971. The government continued to discourage his active participation in politics as he could not run for office in the ___E:1974 general elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_Kenyan_general_election)___ .
In 1982, Odinga attempted to start a new political party - Kenya African Socialist Alliance.
Section 2A of the ___E:Kenyan constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kenya)___ was amended making Kenya a de jure one party state therefore preventing Odinga's efforts.

A coup attempt that same year by ___E:Kenya Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Air_Force)___ soldiers in August, led by a Luo, ___E:Hezekiah Ochuka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hezekiah_Ochuka)___ was foiled. ___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ and his son ___E:Raila Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raila_Odinga)___ were accused of involvement and detained without trial for several months.
These events led to many years of marginalisation of the Luo community.

The perception of marginalisation was further enforced by the murder of ___E:Robert Ouko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Ouko_(politician))___ , the Minister of Foreign Affairs in 1990.  Economic and political marginalisation of the community and disastrous economic management in Kenya, particularly under the KANU party's administration of the nascent state, had tragic consequences for the people of Kenya.

Despite the economic potential of nearby ___E:Lake Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria)___ , Kenya continues to struggle with ___E:poverty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_in_Africa)___ and ___E:HIV/AIDS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS_in_Kenya)___ .

Local and international pressure in the early 1990s resulted in the ___E:Moi government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Daniel_Moi)___ repealing the amendment of section 2A of the constitution.
Multi-party politics was therefore permitted in Kenya.

The ___E:Forum for Restoration of Democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forum_for_the_Restoration_of_Democracy)___ (FORD), a multi-tribal opposition party led by ___E:Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oginga_Odinga)___ , ___E:Kenneth Matiba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Matiba)___ and ___E:Martin Shikuku U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Shikuku)___ was formed.

This party split up due to internal wrangling into ethnic based opposition parties - ___E:FORD-Asili U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FORD-Asili)___ (led by Matiba) and ___E:FORD-Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford-Kenya)___ (led by Oginga Odinga).
Oginga Odinga died in 1994.

___E:Ford-Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford-Kenya)___ later split and Odinga's son, ___E:Raila Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raila_Odinga)___ started the ___E:National Development Party of Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Development_Party_(Kenya))___ (NDP) which had considerable Luo support.
This party merged with KANU in 2002, just before the ___E:general elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Kenyan_general_election)___ .

Raila Odinga is widely credited with enabling ___E:Mwai Kibaki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mwai_Kibaki)___ to win the 2002 presidential election through the support of his ___E:Liberal Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Democratic_Party_(Kenya))___ .

This relationship turned sour however and ___E:Raila Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raila_Odinga)___ led the vote against ___E:Mwai Kibaki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mwai_Kibaki)___ in the ___E:2005 Kenyan constitutional referendum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Kenyan_constitutional_referendum)___ which was widely perceived as a referendum against Kibaki.
More than 1,000 people were killed and 600,000 displaced in the ___E:2007–2008 Kenyan crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%932008_Kenyan_crisis)___ following the 2007 general elections.
The campaign and election period were heavily polarised along ethnic lines.

Raila Odinga led the ___E:Orange Democratic Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_Democratic_Movement)___ against ___E:Mwai Kibaki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mwai_Kibaki)___ 's ___E:Party of National Unity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_of_National_Unity_(Kenya))___ .
A power sharing agreement mediated by ___E:Kofi Annan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan)___ led to a coalition government with Raila Odinga receiving the new position of Prime Minister.
The ethnic rivalry between the Kikuyu and the Luo underscores deeply rooted historical issues that involve access to resources and power.
This rivalry continues to shape Kenya's political trajectory.
Despite the polarised politics that have led to economic and political marginalisation, several members of the Luo community continue to achieve prominence in Kenya.

These include, ___E:James Orengo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Orengo)___ , Professor ___E:Anyang' Nyong'o U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anyang%27_Nyong%27o)___ , ___E:Peter Oloo-Aringo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Oloo-Aringo)___ , ___E:Dalmas Otieno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalmas_Otieno)___ and ___E:Peter Ombija U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peter_Ombija&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .

Dr. ___E:PLO Lumumba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLO_Lumumba)___ who is the former ___E:Kenya Anti-Corruption Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Anti-Corruption_Commission)___ director also is a Luo. ___E:Lupita Nyong'o U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupita_Nyong%27o)___ won an ___E:Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress)___ for her role in the film ___E:12 Years a Slave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12_Years_a_Slave_(film))___ in 2014. Prominent Luo doctors and scientists include the late ___E:Prof. David Peter Simon Wasawo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Peter_Simon_Wasawo)___ , the first science professor in East and Central Africa and first black East African to study and lecture science courses at Makerere university; ___E:Thomas R. Odhiambo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_R._Odhiambo)___ , prominent entomologist, founder of the ___E:International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Centre_of_Insect_Physiology_and_Ecology)___ (ICIPE) and the ___E:African Academy of Sciences U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Academy_of_Sciences)___ , winner of the Albert Einstein Gold Medal (1991); ___E:Washington Yotto Ochieng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Yotto_Ochieng)___ , winner of the Harold Spencer-Jones Gold Medal 2019 from The ___E:Royal Institute of Navigation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_Navigation)___ (RIN) following his outstanding contribution to navigation; ___E:Prof. Henry Odera Oruka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Odera_Oruka)___ , philosopher; Professor ___E:George Magoha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Magoha)___ , a consultant urologist and former Vice-Chancellor of University of Nairobi; and Prof ___E:Richard Samson Odingo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Samson_Odingo)___ , vice-chairman of the ___E:Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergovernmental_Panel_on_Climate_Change)___ (IPCC) which received the 2007 Nobel peace prize.
___E:Tishkoff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tishkoff,_Sarah)___ et al. in 2009 published the largest study done to characterise genetic variation and relationships among populations in Africa.
They examined 121 African populations, 4 African American populations and 60 non-African populations.
Their results indicated a high degree of mixed ancestry reflecting migration events.

In East Africa, all population groups examined had elements of ___E:Nilotic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples)___ , ___E:Cushitic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cushitic_peoples)___ and ___E:Bantu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_peoples)___ ancestry, amongst others, to varying degrees.
They also found that, by and large, genetic clusters were consistent with linguistic classification, with notable exceptions including the Luo of Kenya.

Despite being ___E:Nilotic speakers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_languages)___ , the Luo cluster with the ___E:Bantu speaking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_languages)___ populations that surround them. They suggest that this indicates a high degree of admixture occurred during the southward migration of Southern Luo.  ___E:David Reich's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Reich_(geneticist))___ laboratory also noted similar findings.
They found that mutation frequencies in the Luo were much more similar to those of the surrounding Bantu speakers.
They suggested that Luo speakers in East Africa may not always have been socially disadvantaged as they migrated into territories already inhabited by Bantu speakers.
This is in keeping with oral history, which affirms that large groups of Bantu speakers adopted Luo language, culture and customs that were dominant at the time.
66% of tested Luo men were found to have Y ___E:Haplogroup E-M2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_E-M2)___ (E1b1a) which is common among Bantu speaking peoples.
Traditionally, the Luo people were a patriarchal society with a decentralized government system.
The family was headed by the father or the first wife ( mikayi ) or son in the absence of the father.
Multiple families related through traced ancestry formed a clan ( anyuola ).
Multiple clans together formed a village ( gweng ), headed by a village elder ( dodo or jaduong gweng ).
The village elder ruled with the assistance of other elders who were traditionally men of status gained through commerce, wealth, war, or eloquence.
Multiple villages together formed a sub-tribe ( piny , loosely translated as "tribal state").
A piny was headed by a merit-based hereditary chieftaincy by the eldest son ( ruoth ).
The ruoth was crowned by a diviner ( jabilo ) who was also his spiritual and military advisor.
The Luo government structure was stronger at the state level under the ruoth , who had a council of elders ( galamoro mar jodongo or jodong gweng ), from all the villages in their territory.
The Luos organized their defense and security at the sub-tribe level which was headed by a commander ( osumba mirwayi ), who was part of the council of elders.
The council also had a spokesperson who talked on behalf of the council in official matters in village market meetings, religious, and cultural ceremonies that ruoth presided over.
Sub-tribe relations with each other was ad hoc, as there was no single ruler of the Luo people.
Sub-tribes came together during calamities, war, and natural disasters like drought, famines, and floods to help each other.

Sumo , the act of sharing produce with people who were struck by famine, was a common tradition, with Kisumo being one of the renowned marketplaces where those struck by famine were frequently supported by the generosity of their Luo counterparts.

The concept of a Luo ruler called a ker was coined by ___E:Jaramogi Oginga Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaramogi_Oginga_Odinga)___ during the formation of the ___E:Luo Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_Union_(Welfare_Organisation))___ in 1947 that was aimed at uniting all people of Luo descent in East Africa.

Jaramogi Oginga Odinga was the first Luo ker. As part of distinguishing a tribal leader from a national leader, part of the conditions was that a Luo ker would not go into national politics; when Jaramogi Oginga Odinga went into national politics in 1957, he had to quit being a ker.

In recent years, the Luo ker seat has been claimed by different factions of Luo council of elders that started with the appointment of Willis Opiyo Otondi by ___E:Raila Odinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raila_Odinga)___ in 2010 to replace Ker Riaga Ogalo.
Traditionally, the ker was elected by a Council of Elders and was not appointed as it happened with Opondo Otondi, and a Luo ker could only leave office under two conditions, resignation or death.
Ker Riaga Ogalo argued that he had not resigned nor died to warrant the appointment of another ker, while Opiyo Otondi argued that he was the duly elected ker of the Luo people.

Ker Riaga Ogalo represented Raila in numerous political forums and helped build Raila Odinga's political career contrary to the requirements of the council during the days they were in good talking terms.

Ker Riaga Ogalo is credited for having progressive ideas of all modern Luo kers by championing for circumcision of the Luo men to help in the fight against HIV/AIDS. Circumcision was alien to the Luo tradition but his leadership made many hearts to accept the new changes.
Ker Riaga Ogalo also served as the Vice-Chairman of the National Council of Elders.
During the last years of his reign, he argued that Raila was deterring the Luo people to grow democratically and economically with his style of politics.
Ker Riaga Ogalo died in 2015 after a kidney infection at the Kenyatta National Hospital.

The Council's wrangles continued after his demise with Willis Opiyo Otondi still claiming to be the legitimate ker rivalled by Ker Nyandiko Ong'adi who was elected by the Luo Council of Elders in 2015 to replace ker Riaga Ogalo.

The current ker is Jaduong Odungi Randa, who was crowned on 22 December 2023 to become the ninth Ker of the Luo. Attempts to centralize the Luo people under one authority have not been easy given their history with a decentralized government structure.
Traditionally, the names given to children often reflected the conditions of the mother's pregnancy or delivery (including, for example, the time or season).
Further, the Luos have removed six lower teeth because of lock jaw disease that had affected Luo land

A popular Luo meal includes fish (rech) especially ___E:tilapia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tilapia)___ (ngege) and ___E:omena U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_cyprinid)___ , usually accompanied with ___E:ugali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugali)___ (called kuon in Dholuo) and traditional vegetables like ___E:osuga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_nightshade)___ and ___E:apoth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apoth)___ .
Traditional Luo diet consisted of kuon made of sorghum or millet accompanied by fish, meat, or vegetable stews.

Like many ethnic communities in Uganda, including the Langi, Acholi, and Alur, the Luo do not practice the ___E:ritual U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ritual)___ ___E:circumcision U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumcision)___ of males as ___E:initiation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initiation)___ .
Local churches include Legio Maria , Roho , Nomiya and Fweny among others.
There are Luo Muslim communities, with a notable group living in ___E:Kisumu, Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu)___ .

Historically, couples were introduced to each other by matchmakers, but this is not common now. Like many other communities in Kenya, marriage practices among the Luo have been changing and some people are moving away from the traditional way of doing things.
The Luo successfully expanded their culture through intermarriage with other groups in the region, and many Luo today continue to marry outside the Luo community.
This is mainly acceptable since it is an exogamous community with paternally and maternally restricted at clan level.
The traditional marriage ceremony takes place in two parts, both involving the payment of a ___E:bride price U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bride_price)___ by the groom.
The first ceremony, the ___E:Ayie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayie)___ , involves a payment of money to the mother of the bride; the second stage involves giving cattle to her father.
Often these two steps are carried out at the same time, and, as many modern Luos are Christians, a church ceremony often follows.
Traditionally, music was the most widely practiced art in the Luo community.
At any time of day or night, music would be made. Music was not played for its own sake. Music was functional, being used for ceremonial, religious, political, or incidental purposes.
Music was performed during funerals ( Tero buru ), to praise the departed, to console the bereaved, to keep people awake at night, and to express pain and agony.

It was also used during cleansing and chasing away of spirits.is Music was also played during ceremonies like beer parties ( Dudu, ohangla dance ), welcoming back the warriors from a war, during a wrestling match ( Olengo ), during courtship, etc. Work songs also existed.
These were performed both during communal work like building, weeding, etc. and individual work like pounding of cereals, or winnowing.
Music was also used for ritual purposes like chasing away evil spirits (nyawawa) , who visit the village at night, in rain making, and during divination and healing.
The Luo music was shaped by the total way of life, lifestyles, and life patterns of individuals of this community.
Because of that, the music had characteristics which distinguished it from that of other communities.
This can be seen, heard, and felt in their melodies, rhythms, mode of presentation and dancing styles, movements, and formations.
The melodies in Luo music were lyrical, with a lot of vocal ornamentations.
These ornaments came out clearly, especially when the music carried an important message.
Their rhythms were characterized by a lot of syncopation and acrusic beginning.
These songs were usually presented in solo-response style, although some were solo performances.
The most common forms of solo performances were chants.
These chants were recitatives with irregular rhythms and phrases, which carried serious messages.
Most of the Luo dances were introduced by these chants.
One example is the dudu dance.
Another unique characteristic in the Luo music is the introduction of yet another chant at the middle of a musical performance.
The singing stops, the pitch of the musical instruments go down and the dance becomes less vigorous as an individual takes up the performance is self-praise.
This is referred to as Pakruok .
There was also a unique kind of ululation, Sigalagala , that marked the climax of the musical performance.
Sigalagala was mainly done by women.
The dance styles in the Luo folk music were elegant and graceful.

They involved either the movement of one leg in the opposite direction with the waist in step with the syncopated beats of the music or the shaking of the shoulders vigorously, usually to the tune of the ___E:nyatiti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyatiti)___ , an eight-stringed instrument.
Adamson (1967) commented that Luos clad in their traditional costumes and ornaments deserve their reputation as the most picturesque people in Kenya.
During most of their performances, the Luo wore costumes and decorated themselves not only to appear beautiful, but also to enhance their movements.
These costumes included sisal skirts ( owalo ), beads ( Ombulu / tigo ) worn around the neck and waist, and red or white clay worn by the ladies.

The men's costumes included kuodi or chieno , a skin worn from the shoulders or from the waist respectively to cover their nakedness, Ligisa , the headgear, shield and spear, reed hats, and clubs, among others.
All these costumes and ornaments were made from locally available materials.

The Luo were also rich in musical instruments which ranged from percussion (drums, clappers, metal rings, ongeng'o or gara , shakers), strings (e.g., nyatiti , a type of ___E:lyre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyre)___ ; orutu , a type of ___E:fiddle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddle)___ ), wind ( tung , a horn, Asili , a ___E:flute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flute)___ , A bu-! , to a specific type of trumpet).
Currently the Luo are associated with the benga style of music.

It is a lively style in which songs in ___E:Dholuo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dholuo)___ , ___E:Swahili U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_language)___ , or English are sung to a lively guitar riff. It originated in the 1950s with Luo musicians like George Ramogi and Ochieng' Kabaselle trying to adapt their traditional dance rhythms to western instruments.
The ___E:guitar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar)___ (acoustic, later electric) replaced the ___E:nyatiti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyatiti)___ as the string instrument.
Benga has become so popular that it is played by musicians of all ethnicities.

Luo singer and nyatiti player ___E:Ayub Ogada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayub_Ogada)___ received widespread exposure in 2005 when two of his songs were featured in ___E:Alberto Iglesias U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Iglesias)___ ' Academy Award-nominated score for ___E:Fernando Mereilles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fernando_Mereilles&action=edit&redlink=1)___ ' film adaptation of The Constant Gardener .

Other Luo musicians, in various genres, are ___E:Akothee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akothee)___ , ___E:Suzanna Owiyo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzanna_Owiyo)___ , ___E:Daniel Owino Misiani U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Owino_Misiani)___ , ___E:Collela Mazee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Collela_Mazee&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:Achieng' Abura U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achieng%27_Abura)___ , ___E:George Ramogi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Ramogi)___ , ___E:Musa Juma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musa_Juma)___ , ___E:Tony Nyadundo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Nyadundo)___ and ___E:Onyi Papa Jey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyi_Papa_Jey)___ .
Ocholla Ayayo writes in "Traditional Ideology and Ethics among the southern Luo":
"When the time of the inheritance comes the ideology of seniority is respected: the elder son receives the largest share, followed in the order of seniority.

If it is the land to be divided, for instance, the land of the old grandfather's homestead, the senior son gets the middle piece, the second the land to the right hand side of the homestead, and the third son takes the land on the left hand side. After the father's death the senior son takes over the responsibilities of leadership.
These groups when considered in terms of genealogy, are people of the same grandfather, and are known in Dholuo as Jokakwaro.
They share sacrifices under the leadership of the senior brother.
If the brother is dead the next brother in seniority takes the leadership of senior brother.

The responsibility and prestige position of leadership is that it puts one into the primary position in harvesting, cultivation, as well as in eating specified parts of the animal killed, usually the best parts.

It is the senior brother, who is leading in the group, who can first own the fishing boat. Since it is he who will be communicating with the ancestors of their father or grandfather, it is he who will conduct or lead the sacrifices of religiousity of the boat, as we have noted earlier. [...] The system of the allocation of land by the father while he is still alive is important since it will coincide with the system of inheritance of land. The principle of the division of the land in monogamous families is rather simple and straightforward. [...] The senior son takes the centre portion of all the land of the homestead up to and beyond the gate or to the buffer zone; the second son then has the remainder of the land to divide with the other brothers.

If the land is divided among the elder sons after they are married, and take to live in their lands, it often happens that a youngest son remains in the village of the father to care for him in his old age. His inheritance is the last property, called Mondo and the remaining gardens of his mother. [...] In the case of a polygamous village, the land is divided along the same lines, except that within the village, the sons claim the area contiguous to the houses of their mother.

Each wife and her children are regarded as if the group constituted was the son of a single woman.By that I mean the children of the senior wife, Mikayi, are given that portion of the total area which could have been given to the senior son in a monogamous family.
The sons of Nyachira, the second wife, and the sons of Reru, the third wife, lay claim to those portions which would have fallen to the second and third sons of Mikayi in a monogamous village".

Paul Hebinck and Nelson Mango explain in detail the family and inheritance system of the Luo in their article "Land and embedded rights: An analysis of land conflicts in Luoland, Western Kenya."  Parker MacDonald Shipton also writes extensively about kinship, family and inheritance among the Luo in his book "Mortgaging the Ancestors: Ideologies of Attachment in Africa":

"Outside the homestead enclosure, or (where there is no more enclosure) beyond and before its houses, Luo people have favored a layout of fields that in some ways reflects placements of houses within.

The following pattern, as described in Gordon Wilson's work from the 1950s, is still discernable in our times—not just in informants' sketches of their ideals, but also in the allocations of real lands where space has allowed following suit. If there is more than one son in a monogamous homestead, the eldest takes land in front of or to the right of the entrance, and the second son takes land on the left. The third receives land to the right and center again, but farther from the father's homestead.
The fourth son, if there is one, goes to the left but farther from the paternal homestead than the second.

Further sons alternate right and left. While elder sons might thus receive larger shares than the younger ones, the youngest takes over the personal garden (mondo) kept by the father for his own use—as if as a consolation prize".
